source_title: US Census AI and Early Career Hiring
unit_or_scope: industry-state cells and workers aged 22 to 24
direct_observation: In the most AI-exposed quintile early-career employment declined 12 percent over ten quarters after ChatGPT release and fewer hires were the primary cause; earnings growth slowed slightly
missing_stage: firm adoption task change causality household income local demand and long-run mobility
next_test: match named firms and worker cohorts to adoption tasks training pay hours and household outcomes

direct_observation: Monetary-policy shocks did not explain the rapid relative hiring decline at the most exposed firms but could explain up to one quarter of relative declines through 2025 Q2; pandemic and remote-work trends remain relevant
missing_stage: named adoption-to-worker pathway and local outcome
next_test: compare firms and places with detailed adoption and pre-trend controls

direct_observation: Estimated AI time-value is concentrated toward higher-paid occupations in nearly every country and more strongly in poorer economies; aggregate labor-cost-equivalent depends on scaling assumptions
closed_stage: cross-country distribution signal and measurement boundary
missing_stage: actual pay employment household receipt firm capture service quality and welfare
evidence_status: official working paper using observed usage with explicit scaling caveat
next_test: join country or region usage to workers households firms and local services

unit_or_scope: advanced and emerging economies and occupations
direct_observation: AI-skill vacancies pay more while diffusion can lower employment in high-exposure low-complementarity occupations and pose youth risks; skill imbalance varies across countries
missing_stage: training completion employer absorption mobility bargaining power and household resilience
next_test: follow applicants or worker cohorts from skill acquisition through hiring pay and retention

direct_observation: Regions with more AI-related jobs do not automatically experience overall job growth; AI-skilled workers and some low-skill service workers serving higher earners may benefit
closed_stage: local labor-market counterexample and distribution mechanism
missing_stage: consumption housing business formation service quality and within-place inequality
next_test: compare high-AI regions to matched places on demand housing and service work
